rv.q: The result is a tour de force of family and generational resentment, vividly expressed, often raucously funny, but perhaps too manic to convince in the later stages.
Karis Kelly’s family drama of inherited trauma, which won the Women’s Prize for Playwriting in 2022, shows impressive potential
It is an entertaining work of complexity, humour, horror, and quality.
A very powerful piece showing how difficult families can be and daring to not offer a solution, just an insight into what that must be like.
This emotionally raw piece of theatre is expertly performed as a ‘four hander’ by Julia Dearden as Eileen and the birthday girl.
Karis Kelly's writing is, on the whole, fantastic.
The humour in Consumed may be dark as hell but thanks to a totally committed cast it is a hugely entertaining piece that pulls no punches.
Karis Kelly's Consumed packs a punch, no doubt about it.
Great performances from the four actors in this darkly comic drama exploring the interplay and acrimony between generations.
This is a genius level play not for the faint hearted and will rock the foundations of any family, especially if you have skeletons in the cupboard!
